sections.Aims and Fit of Module: This module aims to provide students with an introduction to business statistics for the non-specialist. The module will provide a broad understanding of the nature of variability and how business statistics can be applied by managers. It will also enable students to derive and understand a variety of graphs and statistics; these skills provide a means for managers to make effective use of statistics in the process of management and decision-making.
sections.Learning outcomes: A. Assess basic mathematical tools and apply them to management field; B. Describe and analyse data, by using frequency tables, frequency distributions, graphic presentation, and different numerical measures; C. Apply fundamental concepts of statistics, including sampling and probability in management context; D. Interpret statistical inference, apply the basic concepts of confidence interval and statistical hypothesis testing; E. Compare the relationship between quantitative variables using simple correlation and regression techniques.
sections.Method of teaching and learning: This module is taught in both lecture and tutorial sessions. Lectures shall include a presentation of the key theoretical knowledge with problem solving examples. Tutorials allow students to discuss the subject matter, and develop their mathematical problem-solving skills under the direction of the teaching staff. It is expected that students spend their self-study time practicing problem solving, using textbook questions, previous years’ exam questions and any other extra material provided by the lecturer. Material is placed in a broad business context, which provides students with an important link between the fundamentals of statistics and their applications for management and decision making.
